newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh urged to move to boost stock market.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh urged to move to boost stock market.

text.p: Bangladesh needs to overhaul its stock exchange, introduce computerised trading and offer fiscal incentives to boost the jittery market, entrepreneurs and experts said.

"Unless there is a strong (stock) market, the industrialisation in the country will face difficulties," Yusuf Abdullah Haroon, president of the Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI), told reporters on Sunday.
Haroon said a conference of stock exchange officials of India, Thailand and Bangladesh on Sunday had produced "useful" suggestions to revitalise Bangladesh's stock market.
Alleged share price manipulations triggered upheavals in the market late last year and hurt investor confidence.
"In view of the deteriorating banking sector the entrepreneurs will not have any other option than to seek financing from the capital (stock) market," Haroon said.
Bangladeshi banks have reported liquidity shortfalls due to huge amounts of unpaid bank loans.

Haroon said delegates to the conference had suggested a year-end deadline for computerised trading on the Dhaka Stock Exchange and the introduction of a Central Depository System (CDS) by the end of 1998.
"All these are prerequisite for transparency in the trading of stocks on the exchange," Haroon said.
The DSE benchmark index shot up to over 3,600 in October from less than 1,000 a few months earlier.
The index was at 1,197.6 at the close of trading on Sunday after shedding 19.08 points, or 1.57 percent, during the session. Friday and Saturday are the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
An inquest by the Securities and Exchange Commission in December found that a large number of brokers and company executives had been involved in price manipulation.
